title: Color Emotions for Multi-Colored Images
research_question: Do people perceive color emotions for multi-colored images in similar ways, and do observer judgments correlate with a recently proposed predictive model for image retrieval?

participants.description: 33 observers (after removing 2 invalid responses) from a group of colleagues, students, and friends, both males and females, ranging from ~20-65 years old, primarily from Sweden.
participants.recruitment: Web address sent to recipients (colleagues, students, friends); not displayed on a public web page for the main study.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Sets of 10 multicolored images (photos and graphics) selected from a database of 5000 images. Samples were chosen based on pilot study judgments to provide homogeneous coverage of the emotion space. Maximum sample size was 70 pixels.

measures.instrument: Interval scaling on a web-based ruler (Cool <--> Warm)
Interval scaling on a web-based ruler (Heavy <--> Light)
Interval scaling on a web-based ruler (Passive <--> Active)
Normalized Root Mean Square (NRMS) deviation between individual observer judgments and the overall mean
Normalized Root Mean Square (NRMS) deviation for judgments of specific samples

measures.construct: Correlation between observer judgments and predictive model
measures.instrument: Pearson product-moment correlation coefficient (r) and coefficient of determination (R²)

findings.consequent: Perception of color emotions (heat, weight, activity)
findings.mechanism: Emotional responses evoked by color content are generally perceived in similar ways across individuals.
findings.quote: The findings of this study show that people in general perceive color emotions for multicolored images in similar ways

findings.antecedent: Predictive model for color emotions (activity, weight, heat)
findings.consequent: Observer judgments of color emotions for multicolored images
findings.mechanism: The model, based on Ou et al.'s single/two-color emotion factors applied to RGB-histograms, accurately predicts human emotional responses to multicolored images.
findings.quote: observer judgments highly correlate with the predictive model recently proposed in image retrieval.

findings.consequent: Observer comprehension and consistency of judgments
findings.mechanism: The activity factor is harder for observers to comprehend and apply on multicolored images, leading to more varying opinions.
findings.quote: the activity factor is harder for observers to comprehend and apply on multicolored images than the heat and weight factors.

findings.mechanism: Images with 'neutral' emotional content (middle of the scale) are more common than 'extreme' content (end points) in both the pilot study and a larger internet database.
findings.quote: Apparently, "neutral" samples... are more common than "extreme" samples

mechanisms: The emotional response to colors in multicolored images can be predicted by a model that transforms ordinary RGB-histograms into emotion descriptors based on psychophysical experiments for single and two-color combinations (Ou et al. model).
The model calculates an expectation vector for each image, representing the mean score for activity, weight, and heat factors.
implementation_implications: The method can be used in image retrieval systems to sort or preselect images based on semantic properties of colors, especially when users are interested in samples with strong emotional content.
The color emotion descriptors can be used for image classification and image indexing.
The method is time-efficient for large image databases as it only involves transformations on RGB-histograms.

tables.description: Pearson r correlation coefficient and R² correlation between observer judgments and predicted emotion values.

limitations: Lack of control over user environment (monitor settings, illumination, background colors, psychological state) when used on public web pages.
Image content (objects, faces, context) other than color can affect emotional response, potentially overriding color-based emotions.
Risk of users deliberately submitting answers disagreeing with their own emotional feelings in anonymous public web tests.
The activity factor is harder for observers to comprehend and apply on multicolored images, leading to more varying opinions.

The selection of samples for the main study, while aiming for homogeneous coverage, might not be ideal for representing the entire target database, which tends to have more 'neutral' than 'extreme' samples.

paper_metadata.title: Color emotions for multi‐colored images
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: AbstractWe investigate the emotional response to colors in ordinary multicolored images. In psychophysical experiments, using both category scaling and interval scaling, observers are asked to judge images using three emotion factors: activity, weight, and heat. The color emotion metric was originally developed for single colors, and later extended to include pairs of colors. The same metric was recently used in image retrieval. The results show that people in general perceive color emotions for multi‐colored images in similar ways, and that observer judgments correlate with the recently proposed method used in image retrieval. The intended usage is in retrieval systems publicly available on the Internet, where both the user and the viewing environment is unknown, which requires novel ways of conducting the psychophysical experiments. © 2010 Wiley Periodicals, Inc. Col Res Appl, 36, 210–221, 2011;
